scenarios: Dependency graph bypass: the parent .scratch/role-assurance/PRD.md says it Blocks the seed, but the seed says Blocked by: none; a graph validator enforcing reciprocal edges must reject this non-reciprocal relationship, so the candidate cannot satisfy its own acyclic reciprocal-graph acceptance.

Bootstrap self-authorization and sibling-contract bypass: the seed authorizes edits to all four sibling packets and says maintainer-only merge is the control, but supplies no machine-verifiable maintainer identity, required-review binding, changed-path digest verifier, or protected-branch transition. A candidate author can therefore alter sibling contract text or statuses while retaining a superficially valid candidate digest and role JSON; prose notes do not enforce the bootstrap boundary.

Stale or forged projection evidence: projection-check.json is a static audit record with an observedAt and headRevision but no independently authenticated remote snapshot or verifier-produced proof. The only fresh issue-sync check attempted here fails with a GitHub connection outage and reports body drift, demonstrating that the checked-in record cannot establish current projection readiness; the seed correctly calls it non-authoritative but does not define a deterministic maintainer rerun artifact/schema before merge.

Weak-agent gaming and dependency errors: the seed requires markdown, diff, finalization, and role-evidence gates but does not name a complete command/schema or an explicit failure code for graph validation, changed-path authorization, and maintainer bootstrap review. A weak implementation can report those gates as passing while omitting the parent-cycle/non-reciprocal check or treating an unavailable remote as success. Existing issue-sync outage behavior cannot compensate for these missing seed-level acceptance controls.
